turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Hi, good to see you both. Zainab, that's a beautiful drawing. Can dad give me your full name and birthday?

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Zainab had it February 14th, 2017. She's a Valentine's baby. I remember.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thanks, Karim. So this is her ADHD follow -up.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: How are things going on the medicine? Honestly, school is way better. She's on the 36 milligrams every morning. Oh no, sorry, it's 27. The 36 was what you said we might try later.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: We went from 18 to 27 milligrams of the long -acting methylphenidate in August. Does she take it every morning?

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Every school day around 7, before the bus,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: weekends too mostly. And how's school going? She's in 4th grade at Riverside Elementary now, right?

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Yes, her teacher M .S.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Kowalski says she's finishing her work and not getting up out of her seat as much. Her reading grade went from a C to a B. That's great to hear. I got the Vanderbilt forms back from both of you. On the teacher form, she has three out of nine attention symptoms now, down from seven in the spring, and the hyperactivity score is down too. Your form looks similar.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Yeah, she's calmer. The only thing is her eating. Tell me about that. She barely eats lunch.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: The lunch comes home basically untouched. Then at four o 'clock, she's starving and eats everything in the kitchen. That's the most common side effect.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: How about breakfast? A little cereal, maybe. She's not a big breakfast person.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, and sleep.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: It takes her a while to fall asleep, maybe 45 minutes. I bought melatonin at the store, three milligrams, and gave it for about a week.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: But she said she had weird dreams, so I stopped it.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: That's fair.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any headaches or stomach aches? No, not really. any ticks like eye blinking or throat clearing now does she seem sad or really irritable when it wears off in the evening a little grumpy right after school but she's herself not sad any fainting chest pain or racing heart especially with running around no nothing like that her brother Omar has ADHD too he takes guan fa seen and he had the same thing with appetite on a stimulant, so I kind of expected it.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: That's helpful.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, her vitals. Blood pressure is 104 over 66, heart rate 94. Her weight is 28 .2 kilograms, and in August it was 29 .0, so she's lost about 0 .8 kilograms, almost 2 pounds. Height is 134 centimeters, so she's still growing taller. Her heart sounds regular, no murmur, and lungs are clear.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Two pounds? Is that a problem?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: It's something we watch, not something to panic about.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: So,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: her ADHD combined type is responding well to the 27 milligrams, and I don't wanna lose that. But the medicine is suppressing her appetite and she's lost some weight. So here's the plan. Keep the methylphenidate at 27 milligrams every morning.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Give it with breakfast and make breakfast bigger and higher calorie,

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: like eggs,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: a smoothie with peanut butter, whatever she'll eat. Pack a snack she likes for lunch, and a real snack after school and before bed.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: On weekends,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: if her behavior is okay, it's fine to skip the dose to let her catch up on eating.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Oh, okay, that's good to know.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: For sleep,

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: screens off by eight,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: same bedtime every night. If she's still taking a long time to fall asleep, we can try melatonin again at one milligram instead of three. Makes sense.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Can you send the prescription to the pharmacy at 2 ,210 Kenwood Avenue?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Yes, a 30 -day supply. Let's have her come in for a nurse weight check on Tuesday, November 24th, and I'll see her in three months. If her weight keeps dropping, we could think about a different medicine, but let's not jump ahead.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: November 24th got it, and if anything comes up, you have my cell, 555 -0147.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Perfect. Keep up the good work, Zainab, and save me one of those drawings next time.
